mechanism: NSAIDs can reduce the antiparkinsonian efficacy of levodopa by inhibiting renal prostaglandin synthesis and increasing sodium/fluid retention, while diclofenac may also inhibit dopamine activity; additionally, both drugs increase GI ulceration risk.
action: Monitor for reduced levodopa efficacy and consider alternative analgesia (acetaminophen, tramadol) or use lowest effective NSAID dose with gastroprotection if diclofenac is necessary.
